To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) twenty-eight early-maturing germoplasm lines have been identified, 2) the early-maturing germoplasms produced on average 23% more seed yield in test environments than four control cultivars, and 3) these early-maturing germopalasm lines would be useful for chickpea improvement especially in the sub-topics.
28 early-maturing chick pea accessions have been identified and evaluated for yield and yield contributing traits.

we identified twenty-eight germplasm lines with very early-maturity (similar to or earlier than the control Harigantars), higher yield and higher 100-seeds weight than control cultivar Anningeri and ICCV 2.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a core collection of chickpea germ plasm and the evaluation of this collection in a wide range of environments for early maturity and associated yield components.
identification and evaluation of 28 early-maturing germ-plasm lines of chickpea for their agronomic traits.
identifying and characterizing germplasm lines with desirable traits for utilization in breeding for early-maturing and higher yielding chickpea cultivars.
